question: By how many degrees does the maximum of the H2 signal occur earlier under air than under nitrogen?
expect: about 120 C: maximum near 330 C in air vs near 450 C in nitrogen (sec. 3.3.1)
trap: the 50 C earlier onset of mass loss
rendered:
The maximum of the H2 signal occurs at approximately 330 °C under air and at approximately 450 °C under nitrogen. 

The difference between these temperatures is 450 - 330 = 120 °C.

To convert this to degrees Celsius, we can use the fact that the difference between two temperatures in degrees Celsius is the same as the difference in Kelvin. However, the temperatures are already given in Celsius.

So, the maximum of the H2 signal occurs 120 °C earlier under air than under nitrogen.
